summary: First live bench of mypintusan, the app that decides who physically walks through a door. It had the thinnest unit coverage in the suite (7 test files) and zero live exercise, and its decision path is a PURE FUNCTION with genuinely good table tests - the shape that lulls, because Decide() can be flawless while the snapshot handed to it is wrong and no test of a pure function will ever notice. tools/fleetbench/pintusan_harness.py stands the app up with a REAL OSDP bus over TCP and tools/osdp-sim on it; tools/fleetbench/bench_pintusan_door.py provisions a site end to end (door, reader, holder, credential, group, schedule, grant) and then presents cards on the wire, asserting only against what the product itself recorded. THE CORE ACCESS PATH HELD UP: 32/32. A valid badge grants and the log names the holder; an unknown card is denied and its raw value still recorded; a revoked credential stops opening the door within one second and is refused for the right reason rather than a generic one; lockdown denies a credential that would otherwise be granted; a duress PIN grants (the door opens for a coerced holder), is recorded as a plain grant with the duress marker only in operator-side fields, and raises a CRITICAL alarm; and a remote unlock is recorded with the operator's name. Two real defects were found and fixed, both small. First, a badge on a reader that ANSWERS PERFECTLY WELL and that nobody has enrolled was filed as reason 'reader-offline' - the one thing it is not. The bench watched a healthy simulated reader deliver cards while the operator was told the reader was offline, which sends whoever is commissioning a new door to check cabling and power for a device whose only problem is that it is not in the database. It now has its own reason code, reader-not-enrolled, mapped and translated in all four languages. Second, in the tooling: tools/osdp-sim's DEFAULT card (deadbeef) fails Wiegand-26 leading even parity, and a CP treats a parity failure as a hard denial because a card one bit out may be somebody else's - so the simulator's own default could never open a door, and the first run of this bench spent itself watching every badge denied. The default is now 00880040 (facility 1, card 4096, valid parity), and the simulator gained a -pin flag so duress is benchable at all: it emits keypad digits BEFORE each card, which is the order the controller requires since it buffers a keypad entry and consumes it when the card arrives.
compatibility: Backward-compatible; no schema change and no configuration change. The reason code on an access event for an unenrolled reader changes from reader-offline to reader-not-enrolled: an operator filtering the events screen for reader-offline will no longer see these rows, which is the point - they were never reader outages. Existing rows already written with the old code are untouched and still render, since the old mapping and its translation remain. The osdp-sim default card change affects bench tooling only, nothing shipped; anyone who relied on the old default getting DENIED should pass -card deadbeef explicitly. Scope is `infra` rather than `mypintusan`: that token does not exist in infra/versioning/version.json's apps map (only myidsan, myiotsan, mymatasan and myseliasan do) and an unknown token hard-fails the release run. Adding mypintusan to that map remains the gate for ever cutting a release for it.
